name: Aligned Data Centers Frederick campus (IAD-04 / IAD-06) at Quantum Frederick

power_mw.unit: MW (four buildings planned; IAD-06 alone is 72 MW)

acres.unit: acres (parcel inside the 2,100-acre Quantum Frederick park)

power_source.value: Grid power; MDE permit to construct (Jan 2025) for diesel backup generators (172 per Nature Forward summary), allowed without a PSC CPCN after the 2024 Critical Infrastructure Streamlining Act

opposition.what: Frederick County Data Center Referendum Committee gathered more than 20,000 signatures to put the Dec. 2025 expansion of the Adamstown data center zone (Critical Digital Infrastructure Overlay Zone) to a referendum; data center companies sued and the Maryland Supreme Court kept it off the ballot (June 30, 2026)

scrutiny.what: Maryland PSC denied Aligned's 2022 request for a CPCN for 168 diesel backup generators; Aligned withdrew until the 2024 law exempted backup generators from CPCN review

news.title: Aligned tops out Maryland data center
Data center frustrations cause upheaval in county primary elections

notes: Land purchase from Quantum Loophole closed 2022-11-29 (company release, used as 'announced'). IAD-04 broke ground Feb 2025; IAD-06 (72 MW, 450,000 sq ft) topped out March 2026. Park is now led by TPG Real Estate / Catellus (Quantum Loophole pushed out 2024); park-wide plan 2.4 GW, 17.4M sq ft entitled (catellus.com).

name: Rowan Bauxite I, II & III campus at Quantum Frederick

power_mw.unit: MW (Rowan sidebar; page body says more than 630 MW)

notes: Rowan's page says Maryland and shows a Frederick image; location at Quantum Frederick per Nature Forward's Sept/Oct 2026 summary. Possible overlap with a separate AWS record if one is created.

name: AWS Calvert Technology Center (Calvert Cliffs)

opposition.what: Change.org petition by resident Melissa Emmal for a data center moratorium, more than 10,000 signatures
Voters ousted all three county commissioners who had voted against a data center pause (June 23, 2026 primary)

news.title: Amazon abandons plans for data center campus at Calvert Cliffs
AWS Withdraws Proposed Calvert County Data Center Project

notes: AWS filed its Conceptual Site Development Plan in May 2026 for 'multiple data center campuses' covering 2.4 million sq ft near the Calvert Cliffs nuclear plant (Maryland Matters, citing a county planning document) and withdrew it on 2026-08-04. On 2026-09-30 Constellation announced a 20-year, 690 MW power purchase deal with Amazon for Calvert Cliffs output that flows to the grid, not to a local data center.

Controversial proposed data center up for debate in Woodlawn

name: Dickerson Data Center Campus (former Dickerson power plant)
owner: Atmosphere Data Centers (Atmosphere Dickerson Property Owner LLC); land from Terra Energy LLC

power_mw.unit: MW (five buildings, scalable; a county council testimony cites 300 MW)

water_use.value: Average 69,300 gallons/day withdrawn from the Potomac River (about 46,200 evaporated); 0 to 500,000 gallons/day depending on weather; MDE withdrawal and discharge applications filed

power_source.value: Grid power from FirstEnergy transmission lines via a new on-site substation (developer pays, over $70M); diesel backup generators (Tier 4, SCR and DPF)

cooling_type.value: Direct evaporative cooling with air-side economizers; river water reused 3-6 cycles

jobs_promised_perm.unit: employees on site (up to, across shifts)

acres.unit: acres (data center site inside the 758-acre former power plant property)

opposition.what: Montgomery County Executive Order 109-26 (2026-06-12) paused data center permit approvals for six months after this proposal; Atmosphere challenged it in court

County Council Bill 19-26E (2026-07-28) set an 18-month moratorium on processing data center permits, and Ordinance 20-35 (ZTA 26-01) prohibits data centers countywide from 2026-08-17 as a bridge to a new framework

news.title: Why the data center industry came to Dickerson

notes: Promoted from lead md-montgomery-dickerson. Terra Energy's conditional use CU202413 (data centers + battery storage, IH zone, 758-acre property north of Martinsburg Road; accepted 2023-12-27, used as 'announced') got a staff approval recommendation for the 2024-09-05 Planning Board and was approved in late 2024 (two buildings). Atmosphere re-filed a major modification CU 24-13(a)(A) for five buildings (Statement of Case 2026-05-26); hearing continued by order 2026-09-01, date TBD. Stage 'blocked': Ordinance 20-35 prohibits data centers countywide from 2026-08-17 with no end date. Address 21200 Martinsburg Rd per developer fact sheet. MW from Nature Forward (cites the developer fact sheet; MW not found in the fact sheet text), so kind 'estimate'. Bethesda Magazine article not opened (403); listed from search result. Official sources: https://montgomeryplanningboard.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/Dickerson-Power-Plant_Terra-Energy-Staff-Report-Final-2.pdf ; https://www.montgomerycountymd.gov/office-zoning-administrative-hearings/hearings/cu-24-13aa-atmosphere-dickerson-property-owner-llc-conditional-use-holder-terra-energy-llc-amendment-major-modification

name: Brightseat Tech Park (former Landover Mall site)
owner: Lerner Enterprises (Brightseat Associates LLC, with The Tower Cos.)

acres.unit: acres (4.1 million sq ft of data center / industrial space approved)

opposition.what: Greater Capitol Heights Improvement Corp. filed a letter opposing the plan as inconsistent with the 2009 Landover Gateway Sector Plan

County Council passed a two-year moratorium on hyperscale data center development, extending the pause; council chair says the county is trying to stop this project

news.title: Lerner's plan for data centers on Landover Mall site advances despite opposition
Prince George's County lawmakers halting data center development

notes: Promoted from lead md-princegeorges-landover-mall. Prince George's Planning Board approved Brightseat Associates' plan unanimously on 2024-03-14 (Bisnow), so it was permitted before the county pause; stage 'paused' while the county moratorium runs. Site was a 1972 Lerner mall demolished in 2006 and an FBI HQ finalist. Data Center Dynamics reportedly says up to 820 MW and $5B across five buildings at 2101 Brightseat Road (https://datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/lerners-maryland-data-center-campus-could-total-820mw), but the page could not be read, so those figures are left out until checked.
